entities.name: Selbach mac Ferchair
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Selbach mac Ferchair (d. 730 CE) was a pivotal figure in early medieval Scotland, asserting the dominance of the Cenél Loairn over the wider kingdom of Dál Riata during a period of intense internecine conflict and external pressure from the Picts. His reign, spanning at least from 701 CE, marked a critical phase in the consolidation of power within the Dál Riatan polity, impacting its future trajectory and relations with neighboring polities. His actions directly shaped the political landscape of Argyll and the western Isles, setting the stage for subsequent power struggles for control over the nascent Scottish kingdom.

Selbach's ascendancy was characterized by aggressive military campaigns documented in the Irish annals. He seized control of Dál Riata by 701 CE, deposing his predecessor, Fiannamail ua Dúnchada of Cenél Comgaill. A significant event was the Battle of Finnchory (Fionnbharr) in 719 CE, where Selbach decisively defeated the rival Cenél Gabráin under Dúnchad Bec, effectively unifying Dál Riata under his control. He also engaged in naval warfare, notably at the "two battles of the Scottish kindreds" in 719 CE, and later undertook a campaign to burn the fortress of Dunollie in 701 CE and again in 713 CE, a stronghold often associated with the Cenél Loairn or a rival faction. In 723 CE, Selbach abdicated and entered a monastery, a common practice for aging kings in this era, ceding the throne to his son, Dúnchad.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Selbach mac Ferchair's reign was critical in the early 8th-century consolidation of Dál Riata under the Cenél Loairn, a period of intense internal conflict and external pressure. His actions, including key military victories, directly impacted the power dynamics of early medieval Scotland and contributed to the kingdom's subsequent vulnerability to Pictish expansion.
